field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.
limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No Jenkins controller was started and no CLI command was sent; the finding is static. The upstream Security3314Test was read, not run.

Jenkins publishes a weekly line and an LTS line whose version numbers interleave: fixed LTS 2.426.3 and 2.440.1 are both numerically below the affected weekly 2.441, while weekly 2.427-2.441 remain affected. A flat Maven range cannot express this disjunction. The two canonical ranges are the advisory's line boundaries (<2.442 weekly, <2.426.3 LTS); a consumer comparing LTS releases against the weekly range can over-approximate fixed 2.426.3/2.440.1.

The CVE v5 CNA record supplies no CVSS and no problemType and encodes the versions with unusual lessThan/status pairs; CWE-22 and the 9.8 vector come from NVD, with CWE-27 from a secondary NVD analyzer.

OSV's GIT 'fixed' endpoints 9ed5f66f and 10b1b883 are the maven-release-plugin prepare-release commits, not the source fixes. The source fixes are a7486539 (LTS) and 554f0378 (weekly), both '[SECURITY-3314]'.
The two source fixes are branch-specific: a7486539 is only in the 2.426.x LTS line and 554f0378 only in the weekly line. Neither is in jenkins-2.441.
The advisory describes what an attacker can read as depending on overall permissions and available CLI commands; no line-count or permission experiment was performed.
The snapshot inventory has 12049 tracked files and 82 ambiguous files; the language job is NEEDS_REVIEW, not a clean PASS.

The fixed-release claim is verified at 2.442, 2.426.3 and 2.440.1. The 2.440.1 tag commit is dated 2024-02-21, after the advisory's 2024-01-24 publication, so the advisory page was revised; the CNA record's dateUpdated is 2024-04-15.

MITRE and NVD copy a description saying unauthenticated attackers can read arbitrary files; the Jenkins advisory limits unauthenticated reads to the first few lines (three in recent releases) and requires Overall/Read for full files. The canonical limitation text follows the advisory.
OSV's affected.versions list contains release candidates and pseudo-versions such as jenkins-2.426.3-rc and builds/341, and omits 2.440.1; it is not used as the range source.

critical_operation.description: Jenkins parses CLI command arguments with args4j. In 2.441 both parser construction sites use default ParserProperties, which leave expandAtFiles enabled: an argument beginning with @ is replaced by that file's contents before the command sees it. CLICommand.getCmdLineParser returns `new CmdLineParser(this)` with no properties, and CLIRegisterer.bindMethod builds `new CmdLineParser(null)` for declarative @CLIMethod commands. The fixed releases add a default-false ALLOW_AT_SYNTAX switch and call ParserProperties.defaults().withAtSyntax(ALLOW_AT_SYNTAX) at both sites, so the @-syntax is no longer expanded unless an administrator explicitly enables it.

entry_point.description: Remote and local CLI commands reach CLICommand.main, which calls getCmdLineParser().parseArgument to bind the argument list. The argument list is attacker-controlled for unauthenticated CLI transports.

trace.description: CLICommand.main receives the argument list and calls getCmdLineParser
main calls getCmdLineParser, which returns a parser with default properties, leaving args4j expandAtFiles enabled
declarative @CLIMethod commands build their parser the same way
args4j replaces @path with the file contents before option binding, so file contents become command arguments

location.verification_method: Static read of CLICommand.java and CLIRegisterer.java at 2.441/2.442, the fix diff, the added test, and release-tag ancestry; no code executed.
